records.name: G.A.R. Civil War Museum & Library
records.summary: A volunteer-run Civil War museum and research library in Holmesburg. Visitors can tour the exhibits, and members and donors can request research help with Civil War veterans and Grand Army of the Republic posts. It does not do family genealogy.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers keep the museum and library open. Visitors can come on a Tuesday or book a guided visit, and members and donors can request research. The site does not describe a volunteer sign-up process.

schedule.text: Open Tuesdays 11 am to 4 pm, or by appointment. Guided visits are booked by email at least seven days ahead. Children under 14 must come with an adult.

cost.text: Touring is free. A membership or donation is suggested: $25 a year for an individual, $35 for a family, and higher levels up to $250. Research requests need a membership or donation.

first_step.how: Come on a Tuesday between 11 am and 4 pm, or email garmuslib1866@gmail.com at least seven days ahead to book a guided visit.
first_step.basis: The museum is open to the public on Tuesdays with no admission fee, and the website says how to visit. The volunteer process is not described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Guided visits are set up in advance with a volunteer guide, so the museum confirms the date after you email. The collection includes Civil War relics, documents and photographs, with displays on Lincoln and on Old Baldy, General George Meade's warhorse. Touring is free, and a membership or donation is suggested.
first_visit_tips: Email at least seven days before a guided visit, with the date, arrival time, number of people, and a contact name and phone number.
Children under 14 must come with an adult.
The site does not describe stairs, an elevator, or parking, so call (215) 613-0350 before you come.

records.notes: Membership amounts come from the membership page. The home page lists Spring 2026 and Summer 2026 newsletter issues without a month, so last_sign_of_life keeps the newest month written (October 2025). The visit and research pages give no hours, stairs, or parking details. The /visit and /contact-us URLs returned 404.

records.name: Great Dames
records.summary: A network for women that runs peer advisory groups, a members' circle, and grant programs for women's ideas. Members meet, learn together and support each other.
records.what_you_do: Join the Circle, apply to an online peer advisory group, or attend public events such as the virtual pitch events and open mic nights.

schedule.text: Peer advisory groups of about 10 to 12 women meet online once a month. Public events are listed by date on the events page.

cost.text: Joining the Circle is done through a PayPal donation link, and no set dues are listed. Peer group fees are not shown.

first_step.how: Apply to a peer advisory group through the online form on the peer groups page, or sign up for a public virtual event listed on the events page.
first_step.basis: Most events are open to anyone, and the site has a clear join link. Peer groups need an online application, and no Circle fee is listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public events are mostly online, usually on weekday evenings starting at 5:30 pm Eastern, and include pitch events and open mic nights where people share stories. Peer advisory groups meet online each month with about 10 to 12 women and a facilitator, and talk about work, family, and personal growth. Circle members get a vote on the yearly grant and early access to some programs.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the date, since many listings do not say whether an event is online or in person.
The Nov. 4, 2026 celebration is in person in Greenville, Delaware, not Philadelphia, and tickets are reserved through a link on the join page.
The peer groups page asks you to confirm cost and availability before you apply, because parts of it may be out of date.

records.notes: The peer groups page footer reads 2018, but its summary PDF is named for 2026, so meeting details may be out of date; the page itself asks visitors to confirm. Event costs and formats are mostly not stated. Older events from 2019 to 2024 were not carried over.

records.name: Green Street Rescue
records.summary: A nonprofit cat rescue in Brewerytown that runs Le Cat Café, where visitors can spend time with adoptable cats, and places cats with foster homes until they are adopted.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat until it is adopted, or visit Le Cat Café to meet the cats. Volunteers work from their own homes on trapping, vetting, and fostering, but the site does not list volunteer roles or a sign-up step.

schedule.text: Le Cat Café hours: Sunday 10 am to 6 pm, Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday 11 am to 6 pm, Friday 11 am to 7 pm, Saturday 10 am to 7 pm. Closed Wednesday.

cost.text: Adoption is $140 for one cat or $200 for two. The site does not show a cafe visit fee or any foster costs.

first_step.how: Fill out the foster application linked on the site. Rescue staff check your references, your landlord, and your vet, then email you when you are approved.
first_step.basis: The home page says cafe visits are by appointment, and the foster page names a clear first step. Fostering needs an approved application.
first_step.what_to_expect: Le Cat Café is the rescue's adoption program, where you can spend time with adoptable cats on Girard Avenue. The rescue calls itself not a shelter: its cats live with volunteer foster homes, and the cafe is where you meet them. The site does not give the visit length or fee, so ask before you go.
first_visit_tips: Street parking is on Girard Avenue, so bring quarters for the meter or use the meterUP app.
The cafe is closed on Wednesdays, so check the hours before you go.
The site does not say whether children are welcome at the cafe, so ask before you go.

records.notes: The home page says cafe visits are by appointment, booked through the cafe's website, but the about page does not say so, and the cafe page (/le-cat-cafe/) returned 404. The booking step and visit fee are therefore unconfirmed. Hours on the home page and foster page agree. The 2022 date is a copyright notice and is not used as evidence. No foster approval timeline or foster supplies are stated.

records.name: Greene Street Artists Cooperative
records.summary: An artist-owned live and work building in Germantown with 15 units, a shared garden, and open studios and events. Members are working artists who buy into the co-op when a unit comes up for sale.
records.what_you_do: Visit open studios and events, join the mailing list for news, or apply for membership when a unit is for sale.

schedule.text: Open studios and events happen through the year. The site does not post dates, so the mailing list is the way to hear about them.

cost.text: Membership means buying a live and work unit and taking over its co-op shares. The only unit listed for sale when we read the site was $130,000 and under contract, and another listing is marked sold.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list on the co-op website to hear about open studios and events, or email greenestreetinfo@gmail.com to ask about the next one.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an artist application and a unit purchase. The public way in is the mailing list and events, but the site posts no dates, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The co-op is a converted warehouse with 15 live and work units on about 1.5 acres, with yards, trees, a garden, and a parking lot. Residents are visual artists, theater artists, and writers, and they share their work through open studios, events, classes, and workshops. Public dates are not posted, so check the mailing list before you plan a trip.
first_visit_tips: Join the mailing list first, since the site does not post dates for open studios.
The site we read does not give a street address or parking details, so ask when you get a date.
If no unit is for sale, you can ask to join the waiting list through the co-op's contact form.

records.notes: No dated 2025 or 2026 event was found on the co-op site, and the one search found no 2026 listing for the co-op. The only 2026 date on its pages is the copyright footer, which does not count. The address 5225 Greene St comes from a third-party wiki page and is not on the co-op pages we read, so confirm it. The same wiki says the co-op takes part in the yearly Philadelphia Open Studio Tours. The 2026 tour runs Oct. 10 and 11 west of Broad and Oct. 17 and 18 east of Broad, but the co-op is not confirmed on this year's list, so the record does not say so. The FAQ page is a general housing co-op explainer and was not used for facts about this co-op.

records.name: Growing Home Garden
records.summary: Two food-growing gardens with individual plots on Mercy Street and Emily Street in South Philadelphia, run with SEAMAAC, which works with immigrant and refugee communities. The gardens were set up to help newcomers grow food from their own cultures.
records.what_you_do: Grow food in an individual plot in one of two shared gardens. Ask the garden contact about getting a plot.

first_step.how: Email gardens@seamaac.org or call (347) 719-1488 to ask about getting a plot.
first_step.basis: The page lists an email and phone number to ask about joining, but it does not say how plots are given out, whether there is a waitlist, or when new gardeners start, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each gardener works an individual plot in one of two shared gardens, which measure about 5,360 and 7,862 square feet. SEAMAAC runs the gardens together with the Neighborhood Gardens Trust and the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society. The pages we read do not describe a first day, work days, garden rules, or costs, so ask the garden contact.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before you visit, since the pages we read do not list open days.
Ask which garden, Mercy Street or Emily Street, has plots open and what the next step is.
The Neighborhood Gardens Trust says demand is high and many of its gardens have waitlists, so ask about a waitlist early.

records.notes: Founding year conflicts: the Neighborhood Gardens Trust page gives 2009 (with preservation dates of 2016 and 2018), and the SEAMAAC page gives 2010, so no founding year is published here. The SEAMAAC update about 150 gardeners is undated and was not used as evidence. The email gardens@seamaac.org was carried over from tier 1 and was not visible in our read, since the page hides it behind email protection. The Neighborhood Gardens Trust garden pages do not name these two gardens.

records.name: Guiding Stars
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that runs youth programs on health and fitness, career and college readiness, and juvenile justice awareness.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in fitness and nutrition lessons, career exploration, resume and interview practice, college application help, and financial literacy classes. The youth work program, C2L-PHL, places young people at partner sites for work experience.

cost.text: The site does not state a fee for its youth programs.

first_step.how: Email info@guidingstars2014.org or use the contact form to ask how a young person can join a program. For the youth work program, C2L-PHL, write to C2L@guidingstars2014.org.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to email or use the contact form, but it does not say who is eligible or what the first step looks like. The youth work program's 2025 applications were closed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first session, where programs meet, or how long they last. The youth work program places young people at partner sites, and its 2025 partners included Mighty Writers, Neighborhood Bike Works, Free to Be Performing Arts Center, and Hunting Park Green. Ask the team what a young person would do in the first few weeks before you commit.
first_visit_tips: The office is at 5356 Chew Ave, Building B, and is open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm.
Call (215) 406-5101 during office hours if you would rather talk than write.
The youth work program is for ages 12 to 24, and the page encourages residents of the Northwest Section to apply, so check that before you apply.

records.notes: Address conflict: the contact page lists 5356 Chew Ave, Building B as the office, while tier 1 had 5226 Ridge Ave from IRS records. Both are kept, and neither is confirmed as a program site. The site names the CEO as both Kimberly Reese and Kimberly Lee, so contact_name stays as tier 1 (from the IRS record) and needs a check. The newest dated item is the C2L-PHL page's 2025 placement partners and closed 2025 applications, with no month, so status stays probably_active. The site does not say where programs meet, and the purpose of its Textedly webform link is not stated.

records.name: Hairs 2 U Wig Bank
records.summary: A nonprofit wig shop in Queen Village. It gives wigs to people who have lost their hair to illness, and it sells wigs and head coverings to everyone else.
records.what_you_do: Book a consultation to be fitted for a wig or learn wig care, or shop in person. The free wig program ships wigs after a hospital doctor or social worker signs the program's patient form. Donations keep the free program running.

schedule.text: Shop hours: Wednesday and Thursday 10:30 am to 5:30 pm, Friday 10:30 am to 6 pm, Saturday 10 am to 5 pm. Closed Sunday to Tuesday.

cost.text: Wigs in the free program are listed at $1 each, plus shipping. Best-selling shop wigs run from about $205 to $3,700 before sale discounts.

first_step.how: Book a consultation at hairs2u.org/consultations. For the free wig program, have your hospital doctor or social worker complete the program's patient form and add the hospital stamp first.
first_step.basis: The shop and consultations are open to anyone, and the site lists hours and an address. The free wig program needs a patient form signed by a hospital doctor or social worker.
first_step.what_to_expect: A consultation is a fitting: the shop says a good fit matters most, and wig sizes run from extra petite to extra large. The shop also offers custom wig making and sells wigs, hats, turbans, and jewelry. The site does not say how long a consultation takes or what it costs, so ask when you book.
first_visit_tips: Book a consultation first, since the site does not say whether walk-ins are welcome.
The shop is closed Sunday to Tuesday, so plan a visit for Wednesday through Saturday.
For the free wig program, get the patient form completed by your doctor or social worker and stamped by the hospital before you contact the shop.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the site published no hours; the contact page now lists them, so the schedule is corrected. The consultations page loaded with no text, so the consultation fee, length, and walk-in rules are unconfirmed, and the tier 1 wording free consultation was dropped. drop_in false is carried over from tier 1 and no page confirms it. The 2020 news article from tier 1 was not re-read and is not cited. The newest dated item is Wig Walk 2025, postponed to spring with no date set, so last_sign_of_life is null. Copyright footers (2024) do not count as evidence.

notes: Seven groups in the batch, all seven written. Searches: 1 of 1 used (Greene Street open studios; no 2026 listing found for the co-op). Fetches: 31 in total, six at most per group. Pages returning 404: garmuslib.org/visit and /contact-us, greenstreetrescue.org/le-cat-cafe/, greenestreetartists.org/events. No blocks, bot checks, or rate limiting. Leads_only items were not fetched or turned into records because this lane covers only the batch groups. Dropped with reason: Neighborhood Gardens Trust is the trust that protects gardens (two of its garden pages were read in part, and it is not a group a visitor joins); Pennsylvania Horticultural Society is a large citywide organization, not a single group; SEAMAAC is a multi-service agency (only its home page was read, and the Growing Home record covers its gardens); the four C2L-PHL partner sites were named but not visited. All are left for future research. Also, one call was made by mistake to a session widget tool that is not a research tool; it returned nothing and changed nothing.
